recommended_approach: Use Mantaflow’s fluid simulation data model by setting up a **Fluid Domain** (API: `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings`) and one or more **Flow** emitters (API: `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings`). For a small fire plume look, the API reference indicates domain-level “noise” controls (e.g., `noise_strength`, `noise_time_anim`) and flow-level noise input (`noise_texture`) that can be used to add turbulent detail/variation to the simulated volume; then apply a suitable volumetric shader setup for fire (note: the provided doc hits did not include a dedicated “blackbody”/fire shading page, only API index references to the fluid settings and noise-related attributes).

domain_settings.noise_strength: `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings.noise_strength` (documented as an attribute in the API index; tune to increase/decrease added noise detail)
domain_settings.noise_time_anim: `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings.noise_time_anim` (documented as an attribute; animate/advance noise over time)
domain_settings.flip_ratio: `bpy.types.FluidDomainSettings.flip_ratio` (documented as an attribute; simulation behavior control depending on solver setup)

flow_settings.noise_texture: `bpy.types.FluidFlowSettings.noise_texture` (documented as an attribute; can be used to drive per-emitter noise variation)
